kaps_punt: Kultuurdiversiteit en morele lesse: Kultuurgroepe in Suid-Afrika; Spyskaarte van verskillende Suid-Afrikaanse kulture; en Morele lesse wat uit die oorvertellings van verskillende Suid-Afrikaanse kulture geselekteer is.

items.bewering: Julle praat een taal aan tafel en eet sekere kos op sekere dae.
items.bron: Brand South Africa / southafrica-info.com, 'Languages that black, coloured, Indian and white South Africans speak': almost all South Africans speak more than one language, even at home; GCIS Pocket Guide to South Africa 2012/13, 'South Africa's People': most South Africans are multilingual. The lesson's own next block gives the example of a mother and father from two different groups, i.e. a home that may well use two languages.
items.regstelling: Klein fout, maar dit word aan elke leerder oor sy eie huis gesê: baie Suid-Afrikaanse huise gebruik meer as een taal aan tafel. Die sin moet nie 'een' taal as die reël stel nie; dit moet ook 'n huis met twee of meer tale insluit. Die tweede helfte (sekere kos op sekere dae) is in orde.

items.bewering: Ouer mense in die gesin het julle daardie dinge geleer. Eendag gee jy dieselfde dinge aan jou eie kinders oor.
items.bron: Essop, G.B. 2017, 'Catching them young: African youth, folktale and the communication of universal moral values', Commonwealth Youth and Development 15(1), Unisa Press (doi 10.25159/1727-7140/3293): oral tradition as 'the main method of passing on beliefs from generation to generation'; UNESCO Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity (2001), preamble, via UNESCO BPI memo 'Cultural Diversity' (2006).

items.bewering: Kultuur is die taal, die kos, die klere, die feeste en die stories van 'n groep mense.
items.bron: UNESCO Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity (2001), preamble, quoted in UNESCO BPI memo 'Cultural Diversity' (2006): culture encompasses 'in addition to art and literature, lifestyles, ways of living together, value systems, traditions and beliefs'; Wikipedia 'Culture' (opening): 'social behavior, institutions, and norms ... knowledge, beliefs, arts, laws, customs ... habits'; Britannica Dictionary 'culture': 'the beliefs, customs, arts, etc., of a particular society, group, place, or time'.
items.regstelling: As omskrywing is die lys gesluit en laat die kern van kultuur uit: die gewoontes en leefwyse van 'n groep (hoe mense dinge elke dag doen) en wat hulle glo en as reg en verkeerd beskou. Die les steun self op albei: blok 'Kultuur se nie hoe jy moet leef nie' se kultuur 'le ook in die gewone dinge wat mense elke dag doen', en blok 'Wat 'n morele les is' se elke kultuur se stories leer reg en verkeerd. Die omskrywing moet minstens gewoontes (die manier waarop 'n groep dinge doen) en oortuigings of waardes byvoeg. As hierdie bewoording 'n gedeelde omskrywing vir die vak is, moet die regstelling daar ook gemaak word.

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika het twaalf amptelike tale
items.bron: SAnews.gov.za, 20 July 2023: President Ramaphosa signed the Constitution Eighteenth Amendment Bill making South African Sign Language the 12th official language; Acts Online, Proclamation 321 (GG 54901, 26 June 2026) and correction Proclamation 324 (GG 54933, 2 July 2026) bringing the Act into operation, and Acts Online news 'Constitution Eighteenth Amendment Act in force' (June 2026): SASL is the twelfth official language in section 6(1). Note: the Act was signed in 2023 but only commenced in 2026; the count of twelve is correct as of today.

items.bewering: en nog baie ander tale daarby
items.bron: Constitution s6(5) as summarised in Wikipedia 'Pan South African Language Board' and southafrica.info: PanSALB must promote the Khoi, Nama and San languages and respect languages commonly used by communities, including German, Greek, Gujarati, Hindi, Portuguese, Tamil, Telegu and Urdu.

items.bewering: Al daardie tale is een teken van hoeveel kultuurgroepe in die land woon.
items.bron: GCIS Pocket Guide to South Africa 2012/13, 'South Africa's People', Languages: 'Owing to its rich cultural diversity, South Africa is a multilingual country'; same chapter lists the cultural groups of the population.

items.bewering: Taal en kultuur is nie dieselfde ding nie. Mense wat dieselfde taal praat, kan heel ander gewoontes en feeste hê.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Cape Malays': the community is today predominantly Afrikaans-speaking and Muslim, while most other Afrikaans speakers are not; Afrikaans-speaking communities therefore keep different religious festivals. Letterkunde.africa, 'Arabic-Afrikaans Literature at the Cape' (Afrikaans written in Arabic script by Cape Muslims).

items.bewering: Baie kinders behoort ook aan meer as een kultuur tegelyk. 'n Ma kan uit een groep kom en 'n pa uit 'n ander groep.
items.bron: HSRC repository record of Jacobson, Amoateng & Heaton 2004, 'Inter-racial marriages in South Africa', Journal of Comparative Family Studies 35: 443-458, which studies intergroup marriage including marriage across linguistic groups and the children of such couples; CBS News 'World of Weddings' (Pedi bride, English-descended groom, lobola negotiated between both families). Marriage across groups is documented; the quantifier 'baie' is broad but not contradicted.

items.bewering: Hulle kind erf dan albei se kos en albei se feeste.
items.bron: No source found that says a child of parents from two cultural groups in South Africa inherits both sides' food and festivals; searched in English for South African studies of mixed-heritage and intergroup families (HSRC, UJ, Cape Town anthropology) and found only that such families exist. Britannica 'Nguni' states that Nguni peoples follow patrilineal descent and virilocal residence (the wife joins the husband's homestead), which suggests that in many traditional marriages the child is counted in the father's line, so 'albei' is not automatic. This turns on South African family practice, where my sources are thin, so I am not contradicting it. The word 'dan' presents as a given outcome what is at most a possibility. A person should decide whether to soften it to a possibility, cut it, or accept it.

items.bewering: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
items.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
items.bron: UNESCO Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity (2001), preamble: culture includes 'value systems, traditions and beliefs'; Wikipedia 'Culture': culture encompasses the 'norms' of a society; Wikipedia 'Cultural universal' (Brown's list): 'Distinguishing right and wrong, good and bad', 'Etiquette', 'Law: rights and obligations'. The lesson itself contradicts the heading in 'Wat 'n morele les is', where every culture's stories teach right and wrong.
items.regstelling: As 'n bewering is die opskrif te sterk. Kultuur lei wel hoe mense leef, want dit dra waardes, reëls en gewoontes. Wat die blok eintlik wys (en wat waar is) is dat kultuur nie alles oor 'n mens se lewe vasle nie, en dat mense in een kultuur nie almal eenders leef nie. Die opskrif moet daardie smaller punt maak, nie dat kultuur niks oor leefwyse se nie.

items.bewering: Mense in dieselfde kultuurgroep leef nie almal op dieselfde manier nie. Een gesin woon in 'n groot stad, en 'n ander gesin woon op 'n plaas. Albei gesinne behoort steeds aan dieselfde kultuur.
items.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
items.bron: Sowetan, 19 May 2020, 'Lockdown has offended African burial rites': Tlokwe Sehume notes that slaughter practice changed because people were living in townships, i.e. members of one cultural group live in town and country and practise differently; Wikipedia 'Basotho blanket': worn by Sotho people in Lesotho and South Africa, with the custom eroding in the capital Maseru but not in rural areas.

items.bewering: Party mense dra elke gewone dag tradisionele klere. Ander mense haal hulle net vir 'n troue of 'n fees uit.
items.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Basotho blanket' and Mmegi (via search): the blanket is part of daily wear for many and is also worn at weddings and ceremonies; Daily News (IOL), 19 Sept 2020, 'Heritage Month: South African cultures and their fashion': the sari is worn for prayers and special occasions like weddings, Swati items are reserved for specific ceremonies, while Punjabi suits and kurtas are worn casually as well as formally.

items.bewering: Kultuur is nie 'n stel klere wat jy net vir een dag aantrek nie. Dit lê ook in die gewone dinge wat mense elke dag doen.
items.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
items.bron: UNESCO Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity (2001), preamble: culture includes 'lifestyles, ways of living together'. The mapping (culture is not a costume put on for a day; it is in everyday life) holds and leads nowhere false. Note that it relies on culture including everyday ways of doing things, which the lesson's own definition of 'kultuur' leaves out (see that item).

items.bewering: Umngqusho word in baie Xhosa-huise geëet en vandag ook ver daarbuite.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Umngqusho': 'Traditionally a Xhosa staple meal', adopted by other groups and 'a staple meal for most South African families' (Zulu: isitambu); Daily Maverick, 6 Sept 2024, 'Let's plan to make Nomalizo's umngqusho for Heritage Day': 'samp and beans, which I (and Xhosa people) call umngqusho'.

items.bewering: Dit is stampmielies en boontjies wat lank saam in een pot gaarkook.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 6 Sept 2024 (Nomalizo's umngqusho): samp and beans cooked together in one pot, two hours if soaked, three to four if not, 'the slower and longer you cook umngqusho, the more delicious it will be'; Sunday Times, 12 May 2013, Dorah Sitole: cook slowly over low heat; Wikipedia 'Samp': the Xhosa umngqusho cooks samp with beans.

items.bewering: Bunny chow kom uit die Indiese gemeenskap van die stad Durban.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Bunny chow': 'originated among Indian South Africans of Durban'; Daily Maverick, 16 Aug 2024, 'Bunny chow love: Durban's unique culinary gift to the world', quoting Desai and Vahed: 'Durban gave birth to a unique dish, the bunny chow', 'an example of Indian inventiveness'. The precise origin story is disputed, but every account places it in Durban's Indian community, which is all the lesson claims.

items.bewering: Dit is 'n stuk brood wat uitgehol en met kerrie gevul word.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Bunny chow': 'a hollowed-out loaf of white bread filled with curry'; National Geographic Travel, 'Where to eat bunny chow in Durban': curry in 'a hollowed-out half or quarter loaf of white bread'.

items.bewering: In Durban bestel mense gewoonlik 'n kwart brood.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Bunny chow': in Durban 'you need only ask for a quarter mutton', and the quarter-loaf size has its own names (kota, skhambane); Daily Maverick, 16 Aug 2024: a bunny 'comprises a quarter or half a loaf'. No sales figures exist, but the quarter is consistently described as the default Durban order.

items.bewering: Bobotie is vandag 'n bekende gereg uit die Kaaps-Maleise kookkuns.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English (dsae.co.za), 'bobotie': 'a traditional dish, probably of Malay origin'; citations credit Malay cooks with bringing it to the Cape and call it 'a Cape Malay speciality'. The earlier origin is disputed (a 1609 Dutch recipe is also cited), and the lesson's careful 'vandag ... uit die Kaaps-Maleise kookkuns' does not claim the origin, so it holds.

items.bewering: Dit is maalvleis met speserye en 'n gebakte laag eier en melk bo-op.
items.bron: DSAE 'bobotie': 'lightly curried minced meat baked with a savoury custard topping'; Saveur 'South African Meat Pie (Bobotie)': spiced meat 'topped with a custard of egg and milk, and baked'.

items.bewering: Party kos hoort by 'n bepaalde dag. Families kook sekere geregte vir 'n troue of vir 'n groot fees.
items.bron: Hombana & Maqajana 2025, 'Meals, identity and othering in Mark 14:12-26', Verbum et Ecclesia 46(1), a3306: in South Africa 'communal meals during rituals such as weddings, funerals and rites of passage' express shared identity; Daily Maverick, 6 Sept 2024: umngqusho made for Heritage Day.

items.bewering: Baie huise het ook 'n Sondagete wat elke week omtrent dieselfde bly.
items.bron: Mail & Guardian, 22 Sept 2023, 'No more seven-colour Sundays': many South African households keep a weekly custom of a feast after the church service ('Sunday kos', 'seven colours'), called 'the weekly ritual'; Eat Out, '5 great 7 colours Sunday lunches in Joburg'.

items.bewering: By 'n begrafnis is kos en saameet dikwels ook deel van die dag.
items.bron: Hombana & Maqajana 2025, Verbum et Ecclesia 46(1): communal meals at funerals in South Africa; Daily Maverick, 14 Oct 2022, 'The rice dish at the end of life': the post-funeral meal at the deceased's home and begrafnisrys; DSAE 'begrafnisrys'; Sowetan, 19 May 2020: slaughter of a cow or other animal as part of burial rites.

items.bewering: Kos is dus meer as net iets om te eet.
items.bron: Hombana & Maqajana 2025, Verbum et Ecclesia 46(1): meals in South Africa 'serving as more than just occasions for physical nourishment'.

items.bewering: Elke kultuur het stories wat ouer mense vir kinders oorvertel.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Cultural universal' (Donald Brown's list): 'Beliefs and narratives' and 'Proverbs, sayings' appear among the universals; Essop 2017, Commonwealth Youth and Development 15(1): oral tradition passes beliefs from generation to generation.

items.bewering: Aan die einde van so 'n storie is daar dikwels 'n les. Daardie deel leer jou iets oor reg en verkeerd, en dit is die morele les.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'moral' (noun): '(of a narrative) The ethical significance or practical lesson', i.e. the lesson of the whole story, not a part of it; Essop 2017, Commonwealth Youth and Development 15(1): folktales rebuke greed and deceit 'through the messages in folktales', which are carried by the story itself. In most oral folktales the moral is not stated as a separate part at all.
items.regstelling: That a story often ENDS with its lesson spelled out is fine (with 'dikwels'). What is wrong is equating the moral lesson with 'daardie deel', a part of the story. The moral lesson is what the story as a whole teaches about right and wrong, whether or not it is spelled out at the end. A learner who learns it as 'the part at the end' will think that a story with no closing lesson has no moral.

items.bewering: Stories uit heel ander kulture waarsku dikwels teen presies dieselfde ding.
items.bron: Thompson, Motif-Index of Folk-Literature (ruthenia.ru edition, section Q): motifs such as Q272 'Avarice punished', Q263 'Lying (perjury) punished' and Q260 'Deceptions punished' are indexed because they recur across the world's folk literatures; Essop 2017: African folktales communicate 'context-specific values, which are nonetheless also manifest in universal values'.

items.bewering: Gierigheid en leuens loop in baie van daardie stories sleg af.
items.bron: Thompson Motif-Index Q272 'Avarice punished' and Q263 'Lying (perjury) punished'; Essop 2017: 'people are rebuked for human foibles such as pride, greed, corruption, and deceit'. 'Baie' rather than 'alle' is correct: in trickster tales (for example Jakkals en Wolf, from Khoi oral tradition per Van Niekerk 2018, Tydskrif vir Letterkunde) the lying trickster often wins, so any widening to 'all' or 'always' would be false.

items.bewering: As jy ander kulture se kos proe en hulle stories hoor, leer jy die mense beter ken. Dit help jou om te respekteer waarin hulle van jou verskil.
items.bron: Essop 2017, Commonwealth Youth and Development 15(1), 'Folktale as intercultural communicative tool'; UNESCO BPI memo 'Cultural Diversity' (2006): culture as 'an innovative arena for dialogue and mutual understanding'. This is a value statement more than a fact, and nothing contradicts it.

items.bewering: Die taal, kos, klere, feeste en stories wat 'n groep deel.
items.bron: UNESCO Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity (2001), preamble: 'lifestyles, ways of living together, value systems, traditions and beliefs'; Wikipedia 'Culture': 'norms ... beliefs ... customs ... habits'; Britannica Dictionary 'culture': 'the beliefs, customs, arts, etc.'.
items.regstelling: Same fault as the definition in 'Wat kultuur is', and a glossary entry is read alone: a closed list of five things that leaves out a group's customs or way of life and its beliefs or values. The entry must include at least customs (how the group does things) and beliefs or values. The two definitions should stay identical.

items.bewering: 'n Groep mense wat baie van dieselfde gewoontes en stories deel.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary 'culture' (count sense): 'a particular society that has its own beliefs, ways of life, art, etc.'; Dutch reference sources: 'een groep mensen met dezelfde waarden, normen en gewoonten'. The hedge 'baie van' is correct, because members do not share everything (as the lesson itself says).

items.bewering: 'n Taal wat die land se wette en regering amptelik erken.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Official language', citing Cambridge: 'the language or one of the languages that is accepted by a country's government ... used in the courts of law'; Constitution s6(1) lists South Africa's official languages (SAnews, Acts Online).

items.bewering: Iets wat mense al baie lank op dieselfde manier doen.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'traditional': 'Of, relating to, or derived from tradition', 'Communicated from ancestors to descendants'. The simplification leaves out the handing-down from one generation to the next but does not cross into falsehood. The first block of the lesson carries the handing-down.

items.bron: Same as the study-block item: Daily Maverick, 6 Sept 2024; Sunday Times, 12 May 2013 (Dorah Sitole); Wikipedia 'Umngqusho' (samp and sugar beans).

items.bron: Wikipedia 'Samp': 'dried corn kernels that have been pounded and chopped until broken', 'The coating around the kernel loosens and is removed during the pounding and stamping process', and 'This food is called "stampmielies" in Afrikaans'; DSAE 'stamped mealies' (Lamont 1910): 'mealies from which the outer husk has been removed', stamped with a heavy wooden stick.

items.bron: Wikipedia 'Bunny chow' (hollowed-out loaf filled with curry; quarter, half and full sizes; 'quarter mutton' as the standard Durban order); National Geographic Travel (half or quarter loaf).

items.bron: DSAE 'bobotie': 'lightly curried minced meat baked with a savoury custard topping'; Saveur: topped with a custard of egg and milk and baked.

items.bewering: Die deel van 'n storie wat jou oor reg en verkeerd leer.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'moral' (noun): '(of a narrative) The ethical significance or practical lesson'; Essop 2017: values are carried 'through the messages in folktales'.
items.regstelling: A glossary entry is read alone, and this one defines the moral lesson as a PART of a story. It is the lesson about right and wrong that the story teaches, whether or not a closing sentence spells it out. Defining it as 'die deel' tells a learner that a story with no stated moral has none. This should match the corrected wording in 'Wat 'n morele les is'.

opsomming: Every food fact checks out (umngqusho, bunny chow and the Durban quarter loaf, bobotie, samp), as do the twelve official languages (South African Sign Language came into force in June 2026). There are no superlatives in the lesson. But the definition of culture, in the study text and in the glossary, is a closed list (language, food, clothes, festivals, stories) that leaves out customs and beliefs or values, which the lesson itself relies on later; the heading 'Kultuur se nie hoe jy moet leef nie' overclaims, since culture carries norms of right and wrong, as the lesson's own moral-lesson block says; the moral lesson is defined as a 'part' of a story rather than the lesson the story teaches; and 'Julle praat een taal aan tafel' does not fit many multilingual South African homes. A person must decide on one claim no source settles, that a child of parents from two cultural groups inherits both sides' food and festivals ('erf dan'), which is stated as a given although in patrilineal Nguni custom a child traditionally belongs to the father's line.
